title: Led around the fire
hookLine: a couple ties a knot and walks around a fire. the Rig Veda's wedding hymn says why: the bride is led around Agni first
carry: agni, the fire, is witness to the wedding vow
tomorrow: The hymn that quotes its doubters
last: ONE VERSE, SEEN FROM SIX SIDES.

lines: A KNOTTED SCARF. A SMALL FLAME.
A WEDDING IN THE RIG VEDA.
cards: A wedding hall. A small fire in a square of bricks, a priest chanting, and a couple, tied together by a knotted scarf, walking slowly around the flame while the family throws rice and petals.

Somebody's little cousin asks the obvious question: why are they walking around a fire? The answer goes back to a wedding in the Rig Veda, and the bride is the daughter of the Sun. This week, four of the Veda's voices.
Today: Agni, the fire, at a wedding.

teach.b: The Rig Veda's wedding hymn, book ten, hymn eighty-five, tells of the marriage of Surya, the daughter of the Sun. In paraphrase: her mind was her wagon, the sky its canopy, and two bright oxen drew it.
Soma, the moon, was the groom, and the Ashvins, the twin horsemen gods, rode along as the wedding escort. A wedding with the whole sky invited.
Then the hymn comes down to the ground, to a human wedding, and the god it turns to is Agni.
In paraphrase: to you, Agni, they first led Surya around, with her bridal train. Give the wife to her husband, Agni, with children to come. The bride is led around the fire first.
Agni receives her and gives her into her new life.

teach.h: "I TAKE YOUR HAND FOR GOOD FORTUNE."
teach.b: Another verse is the groom's: I take your hand for good fortune. Verses from this hymn are still recited at many Hindu weddings. Here's the teaching.
In the Vedas, Agni is the go-between: what is placed in the fire reaches the gods. So a promise made beside the fire isn't made only to a spouse. It's made in front of the gods, with Agni as witness.
That's why Hindus marry before a sacred fire and walk around it, the rounds many families call the pheras.
People call such a marriage agni sakshi: with fire as witness. The flame isn't decoration. It's the guest who carries the vow up.

how: At many Hindu weddings the couple walks around a sacred fire while verses are chanted, some of them from the Rig Veda's wedding hymn (10.85), with Agni treated as witness to the vows.

games.q: you're at Surya's wedding in the hymn. before she goes to her new home, where is she led?
games.why: to you, Agni, they first led Surya around. the fire receives her and gives her into her new life, and the vow is witnessed.

practice: If you can, light a diya or a candle, safely, and sit where you can see it; if not, picture a wedding fire you've seen. Bring to mind one promise you've made, to a person, to God, or to yourself.
Say it quietly in front of the flame, as if Agni were listening and carrying it up. If you pray, ask for help keeping it. If you don't, let the flame simply be your witness.

wordCard.voice: Hymns to Agni. Today, Agni at the wedding: the fire the bride is led around first, witness to the vow. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit and Hindi: witness. A marriage made before the fire is called agni sakshi, with fire as witness.
